findings.finding: The plan states 'Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50' as the effective server page size for `jira.search.views.default.max`, but this is factually incorrect per Atlassian's own documentation. The 50-issue figure is the response size when maxResults is omitted entirely from the request. When maxResults is passed (as both `_paged_search` and `_iter_pages` do — passing 100), the server honors the request up to `jira.search.views.default.max`, whose documented default is 1000. An implementer reading the plan's claim may seed only 2*50+1=101 issues expecting to exercise three pages of 50, when the actual pager (_paged_search uses page_size=100, _iter_pages uses page_size=100) would fetch all 101 in a single page — exercising zero pagination. The 'observe first' instruction partially mitigates this, but a wrong expectation anchors the implementer's interpretation of what the observation means.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — pagination bullet: 'Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50, but `jira.search.views.default.max` is server-configurable and the server silently truncates'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50' with: 'the pager requests page_size=100; the server cap `jira.search.views.default.max` defaults to 1000 but may be lower on this harness — the observation step will tell you the effective cap'. Seed at least `2 * observed_page_size + 1` using the value returned by the observation call (where observed_page_size is the batch length from a single `search_issues(maxResults=page_size)` call), which is what actually determines how many pages are required.

findings.finding: The idempotence AC ('a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing') specifies no observable or oracle, leaving it satisfiable by the exact tautological pattern — checking exit code 0 or the 'OK: steady-state' line — that this story was explicitly created to end. The plan's own founding diagnosis ('converged and works are indistinguishable' on empty input) applies equally here: a pass that finds nothing to do is indistinguishable from a pass that correctly found nothing left to write, unless the assertion reads the dry-run plan and verifies zero mutations of the type exercised.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — '[ ] a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing (idempotence)'
scenarios: An implementer runs the second pass and checks exit code 0 or the stderr 'OK:' line — the test is green but has proved nothing; a regression that emits a spurious write on the second pass goes undetected.

findings.suggested_fix: For each direction, run the repeated pass as `--mode dry-run`, capture stdout, and assert via jq that the plan array contains no mutations of the relevant direction and action (excluding probes). findings.finding: The plan's required-sequencing note for row 14 states 'A binding must therefore exist BEFORE the issue is deleted' to trigger the (inbound, probe) mutation. findings.finding: The `bound_dc_issue` fixture specifies 'a WRITING-MODE inbound pass' (step 2) but there is no inbound-only mode in the codebase: every writing mode (`bootstrap-strict`, `bootstrap-throttle`, `live`) runs both inbound AND outbound differs via `run_differs._run_differs_outbound`. With ~1000 unbound local tickets in the scrubbed store and no `--filter-local-ids` specified for step 2, the outbound differ routes every unbound ticket to the CREATE path (`outbound_differ.py:518-520`). `bootstrap-strict` (cap=10, `mode.py:106`) applies 10 mutations, creating 10 spurious harness issues from production store content; `live` applies all ~1000. This directly violates the plan's own rule ('the only UNFILTERED pass is the scrub-verification dry-run') and destroys the harness isolation the fixture exists to preserve — the created issues are production ticket data seeded into the test harness.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR OUTBOUND ROWS 2-13' — `bound_dc_issue` fixture definition, step 2: 'runs a WRITING-MODE inbound pass so the local ticket and its binding exist'

Then assert `bindings.get_jira_key(expected_local_id) == dc_key` before yielding. This scopes the pass to the single newly-created issue, leaving all other store tickets untouched.
